name: inprocess-obi-apb-pulp-spi-fuzz
notes: One OBI CPU (Ibex) and the pinned PULP apb_spi_master APB3 register target (profile configs/peripherals/inprocess_verify_pulp_spi_irq, the same pinned RTL as configs/peripherals/pulp_spi plus the one declared EOT interrupt source); no DMA model is declared, so F6 is refused by name (unsupported-f6:no-dma-model:APB)

the target window is the same 4 KiB APB window at 0x40001000 already used by configs/scenarios/inprocess-verify-irq-pulp-spi-f1f6.json; the register map is the profile's ten words (STATUS 0, CLKDIV 4, SPICMD 8, SPIADR 12, SPILEN 16, SPIDUM 20, TXFIFO 24, RXFIFO 32, INTCFG 36, INTSTA 40) and is not repeated here

the four SPI data inputs sdi0..sdi3 are held at 0 by the declaration's fixed_inputs; the generic APB3 register template owns every non-bus input, so leaving them undeclared would be refused rather than defaulted. The same four rows are written to source_tuning.fixed_inputs because the entry consumes the header constants and the generated harness request separately

F5 facts are not repeated inline: source_behavior names configs/behaviors/pulp_spi_eot_f5.json, which declares events_o[1] EOT, 16 ticks, trigger writes [[16,65536],[24,171],[0,2]], status word offset 40 (INTSTA) and no cause bits/clear writes. Those are the same facts already recorded for this RTL in configs/scenarios/inprocess-verify-irq-pulp-spi-f1f6.json

the interrupt source is a one-cycle pulse (profile interrupts[0].trigger=pulse), so the host stretches it to the declared 16 ticks; the ISR reads INTSTA at 0x28, whose profile notes say that offset has no read-mux arm, so the status word is declared while cause bits are not
the cpu and target declare 50 MHz, so assume_single_clock states that one host tick drives both models
fuzz mode: f1_program_words 4 declares a four-word straight-line F1 program in the fixed trampoline slot, and the bounded handler wait is 128 iterations
